events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Why, what a MAGNIFICENT entrance hall! I declare, I have never seen such a splendid chandelier — even if it does look like it might come crashin' down at any moment! Oh my stars and garters, is that a guest book? A proper lady always checks the guest book — you never know WHAT kind of secrets previous visitors might have left behind!

The Doily Diamond is somewhere in this mansion, and I intend to find it before the night is through. But first — always start with the details, Clara. The guest book could be the very first breadcrumb on the trail!
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Ah-HA! Ladies and gentlemen, what a MAGNIFICENT entrance hall! Now, I happen to have it on VERY good authority — a letter from the late Lord Doily himself, you understand — that the treasure is hidden deep in the KITCHEN! Yes, yes, the kitchen! Behind the wood-burning stove, if I recall correctly. You should ALL rush there at once! Every last one of you! Dastardly — I mean, Foxworth — NEVER lies! Mehehehe!

The treasure is OBVIOUSLY not in the kitchen — I just made that up on the spot! While these gullible fools stampede toward the copper pots and pans, I shall investigate the library. A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? That SCREAMS 'hidden treasure' to anyone with half a brain cell! Which, fortunately for me, eliminates most of the competition. Oh, I am BRILLIANT! Absolutely BRILLIANT! Soon that treasure will be mine, and perhaps I'll finally earn a REAL medal to replace this fake one!
Dick Dastardly examined the null.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, esteemed guests, to Doily Manor! I am Mr. Pemberton, humble estate manager, entirely at your service. Do forgive the dust — the manor has been... between housekeeping staff, shall we say. If anyone requires anything at all — a cup of tea, directions to the powder room, a tour of the grounds — you need only ask your devoted Mr. Pemberton. Now then, I do believe I shall ensure everything is in order for your stay. One must be thorough, mustn't one?

They smile at me. They nod politely. Little do they know that behind this obsequious mask lurks Vincent Marsh — and Vincent Marsh has PLANS. Oh yes, deliciously elaborate plans! But first — where is Clara Bellingham? She must be somewhere in this decrepit pile. I must find her before she finds the treasure, and then... well. Accidents happen in old manor houses, don't they? Chandeliers fall. Staircases crumble. Such a TRAGEDY it would be. But patience, Vincent, patience. The game has only just begun!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the null.

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell has arrived! And what a magnificent — if somewhat neglected — establishment this is. The chandelier alone speaks of grandeur, though it does hang at a rather alarming angle. Now then, a true gentleman always signs the guest book. It is the DONE thing. And while doing so, one might glean who else has graced these halls with their presence. Preparedness, ladies and gentlemen, is the cornerstone of gallantry!

My heart is positively THUNDERING with anticipation. Clara must be somewhere in this manor. I must find her before some scoundrel gets the chance to impress her first. But patience, Hartwell — survey, strategise, then SWEEP her off her feet with your impeccable heroism. The guest book first. Intelligence before action. Well... intelligence before MOST action.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey, lads, would you look at this place! Fallin' apart at the seams, it is! That chandelier up there could drop on someone's bonce any second — and there's dust thick enough to choke a horse! Right then, everybody stay sharp! We got a job to do, ain't we? Keep our eyes peeled for anything dodgy. And there's plenty dodgy about this manor, I can feel it in me bones!

The lads and me, we ain't the sharpest tools in the shed, but we know trouble when we smell it. And this place REEKS of trouble. That Sneekly fella... there's somethin' wrong about 'im. The way 'e smiles, like a cat what's already got the canary between its teeth. I just can't figure out WHAT it is about 'im that puts the wind up me.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Dick Dastardly: Well, what are you all STANDING around for?! I just told you — the treasure is in the KITCHEN! Chop chop! Time is of the essence! I, meanwhile, shall... er... stand guard here in the entrance hall. Yes! Guard duty! Someone has to protect the rear flank, after all! Very important tactical decision! Now GO, all of you!

The moment these gullible fools turn their backs, I'm slipping into that library faster than Muttley can snicker! That inscription on the mantelpiece is practically BEGGING to reveal the treasure's location. Oh, Dastardly, you magnificent schemer — you've OUTDONE yourself this time!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I NEVER! A guest book in a mysterious mansion and I barely gave it a glance? Clara Bellingham, where are your MANNERS? Let me take a proper look at this — every name, every date, every little scribble could be a clue to the Doily Diamond! Why, the answer might be written right here in plain sight, and wouldn't THAT just be the cat's pajamas!

My heart is absolutely RACING with excitement! The library has an inscription on its mantelpiece that sounds positively riddlesome — and if there's one thing I adore, it's a good riddle. But first things first, sugar. Never skip the obvious clue right in front of your pretty little nose.
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): If you'll pardon me, dear guests, I must attend to the other rooms — ensure everything is shipshape for your treasure hunt! The Library in particular has been dreadfully neglected, and I should hate for anyone to be injured by a falling volume. Do be careful with that chandelier, won't you? It's been rather temperamental of late.

The Library — YES! If Clara Bellingham is there, surrounded by towering shelves of ancient tomes, the possibilities for a theatrical demise are ENDLESS. A bookcase toppling like a domino! A secret passage sealing shut! Oh, Vincent, you magnificent schemer, you are WASTED on this provincial estate management charade. But patience — the mask of Pemberton serves its purpose. No one suspects the butler. Well, estate manager. CLOSE ENOUGH.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — and I use the term generously for SOME present — James Hartwell shall now proceed to the Library! For it is in BOOKS, not kitchens, that the secrets of great houses are kept. Any fool can rummage behind a stove, but it takes a man of LETTERS to decode an inscription carved in stone! And should anyone — particularly anyone of a refined and gracious disposition — wish to join me, I would consider it the HIGHEST honour to serve as escort and protector through these dusty corridors. The chandelier, I note, is swaying most alarmingly. Hartwell is ON it.

Clara, wherever you are in this manor, James Hartwell is coming. And he shall arrive with ANSWERS, with COURAGE, and with impeccably polished boots. The Library first — deduction before devotion. Well... deduction AS devotion.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: Ah-HA! The mantelpiece! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, that's ELEMENTARY! It's a MAP! A MAP, I tell you! The answer is so obvious it practically SCREAMS at anyone with half a brain cell — which, I note, excludes MOST of the guests in this dreary manor! Now then, let us see what secrets you yield to a mind of SUPERIOR intellect!
The Slag brothers are watching, but it doesn't matter — by the time their two collective brain cells process what I'm doing, I'll have found the treasure and be halfway to the exit! Mwehehehe!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, sugar plums, that guest book was just DELIGHTFUL — names going back AGES! But I do declare, my curiosity is pulling me toward that library like a magnet to a hatpin! A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? Why, that has RIDDLE written all over it, and if there's ONE thing Clara Bellingham knows, it's how to unravel a good riddle! Mr. Foxworth, darlin', you go right ahead and guard this entrance hall — what a BRAVE and selfless thing to do! I'm sure the kitchen is lovely, but a girl's got to follow her instincts, and mine are saying LI-BRA-RY!

Oh my stars, I am just BUZZING with anticipation! Every fiber of my being is telling me that inscription holds a clue to the Doily Diamond. Dick Dastardly wanting everyone in the kitchen while he 'guards' the entrance hall is just him being his helpful self, I'm sure. But Clara Bellingham didn't come all this way to look at copper pots — I came to solve PUZZLES!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi oi oi! 'Old up a minute, everyone! Did you 'ear that Foxworth geezer? 'Rush to the kitchen,' 'e says! 'Behind the stove,' 'e says! Since when does anyone just TELL you where the treasure is?! That's fishier than Billingsgate Market on a Monday mornin', that is! Nah, nah — the lads and me, we ain't fallin' for that one. We're stayin' RIGHT 'ERE where we can keep an eye on things. And by things, I mean... well... EVERYTHING. This whole manor gives me the willies, it does!

The lads are gettin' nervous, I can tell. Big Tony's crackin' 'is knuckles, Little Artie's eyes are dartin' about like a pinball machine. But we made a promise, didn't we? Keep Clara safe. And I got this feelin' — deep in me gut, where the pie and mash sits — that somethin' terrible is bein' planned for 'er. That Foxworth wants everyone in the kitchen... and that Pemberton bloke is watchin' Penelope — I mean Clara — like a hawk watches a field mouse. I can't prove nothin'. I'm not exactly Sherlock bloomin' 'Olmes. But me gut's never wrong. Well... it's SOMETIMES wrong. But not today!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome to the Library, distinguished guests! Do mind your step — the dust is rather treacherous on the floorboards. I'm just going to see about these bookshelves, if you don't mind. Several volumes appear to be shelved upside down — most irregular! The late Lord Bellingham would be SPINNING in his crypt. Let me just... inspect the state of things.

The bookshelves! Those glorious, towering monuments to KNOWLEDGE and DESTRUCTION! If even ONE shelf is loose — if the brackets have rusted, if the wood has warped — then all it takes is a gentle nudge at the right moment, and AVALANCHE! An avalanche of leather-bound literary justice! But I must be CAREFUL. Pemberton would fuss over upside-down books. Vincent Marsh checks load-bearing integrity. Same action, VERY different motivations. Oh, I am DIABOLICAL!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: AH-HA! The Library! Just as I suspected — a place of MYSTERY and INTELLECTUAL CHALLENGE! And what have we here upon the mantelpiece? A riddle, carved in STONE no less! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Well, well, WELL! James Hartwell did not graduate top of his class in Absolutely Nothing Relevant to stand here BAFFLED! The answer, my good fellows, is a MAP! A map has cities, forests, and water — but none of the REAL things! If this manor has hidden its secrets behind wordplay, then it has chosen the WRONG adversary! Now let us see what happens when a gentleman of action ENGAGES with this inscription!

My heart is POUNDING with the thrill of deduction! Oh, if only Clara were here to witness this moment — James Hartwell, solver of riddles, decoder of stone inscriptions, CHAMPION of the intellectual arts! I must remember to retell this moment to her with appropriate dramatic embellishment. Which is to say — exactly as it happened, because it IS dramatic.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Yes, YES! Just as I suspected — the inscription confirms it! The treasure is hidden in the LABORATORY! Something about brass instruments and a machine with many levers — one of those levers OBVIOUSLY opens a secret vault! You'd better hurry before someone ELSE figures it out! I'm FAR too busy with important scholarly research here to bother with lever-pulling. Go on, OFF with you! Shoo! SHOO!

Mwehehehe! Send them all scrambling to the laboratory like rats chasing cheese! Meanwhile, those upside-down books on the shelves are practically WAVING at me — 'Look here, Dastardly, look HERE!' A hidden map, a secret compartment, a treasure clue disguised as literature — oh, the GENIUS of it! While those dimwits are pulling levers and getting electrocuted, I shall be one step closer to GLORY and MEDALS!
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, HELLOOO, library! Oh my gracious, would you just LOOK at this place — books from floor to ceiling, dust thick enough to write your name in, and THAT magnificent mantelpiece! Now let me see here... 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, sugar, that's as clear as a Georgia sunrise! It's a MAP! Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish — all drawn on paper but none of it REAL! James, darlin', I do hope you won't mind that I got to it first — a girl simply CANNOT resist a good riddle!

My heart is just POUNDING! If this riddle unlocks something — a hidden compartment, a secret passage — it could lead straight to the Doily Diamond! And with all these lovely people around to share the adventure with, why, it's practically a PARTY!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads — EMERGENCY MEETIN'! Clara's gone to the library, ain't she? And who's followed 'er in there? EVERYONE dodgy, that's who! Foxworth, Pemberton, that Hartwell bloke — she's surrounded! Now I can't put me finger on EXACTLY what's wrong, but somethin' about this whole setup stinks worse than Big Tony's trainers after a bank job! We're movin' out — formation delta, lads! That means everyone follow me and try not to knock nothin' over! ...I KNOW we always knock somethin' over, but let's at least TRY! Clara needs us, and The Ant Hill Mob does NOT leave a lady unprotected!

Me 'eart's poundin' like a drum in a brass band. I don't know what's waitin' in that library, but I know this much — if anythin' 'appens to Clara while I'm stood 'ere readin' a guest book, I'll never forgive meself. The guest book didn't tell me nothin' useful anyway — just a bunch of posh names and dates. Me readin' ain't exactly top-notch at the best of times. But me INSTINCTS? Me instincts are screamin' louder than Little Artie when 'e sees a spider. Library. NOW.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Miss Bellingham! How fortuitous that you've arrived! I was just tidying these shelves and I noticed something most peculiar — several of these volumes are shelved upside down, and they appear to be arranged in a PATTERN. Your late uncle was rather fond of book ciphers, if memory serves. Perhaps you'd care to take a closer look? I confess my old eyes aren't what they used to be, and the upper shelves are quite beyond my reach without the stepladder — which, I'm afraid, has seen better days.

YES, come closer, Clara dear! Come inspect the upper shelves where the brackets are WEAKEST! One little tug on the right volume and the whole magnificent edifice comes crashing down like the walls of Jericho! And when they investigate? A tragic accident — old house, neglected maintenance, such a SHAME about poor Miss Bellingham! The estate manager TRIED to warn everyone about the dust! Oh, Vincent, you are a GENIUS wrapped in a cardigan!

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham! What FORTUITOUS timing! You arrive at the very moment James Hartwell has CRACKED the riddle of the mantelpiece! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — the answer, my dear lady, is a MAP! A map of these very grounds, I'll wager! And NOW — observe those bookshelves! Several volumes shelved UPSIDE DOWN? That is no accident! That is a SIGNAL! When a riddle points to a map and books are inverted, it means someone has HIDDEN something among those shelves — and James Hartwell intends to find it! Stand back, everyone — particularly you, Sneekly, there's a good fellow — and allow a gentleman of ACTION to conduct a THOROUGH examination!

My heart is doing somersaults! She is HERE, she is watching, and I have just delivered the most MAGNIFICENT display of deductive reasoning since — well, since ever! Now if I can just find the map in those bookshelves before Dastardly or that peculiar estate manager gets to it, Clara Bellingham will have no CHOICE but to be thoroughly impressed. James Hartwell, you magnificent devil — this is YOUR moment!
Peter Perfect examined the bookshelves.

Dick Dastardly: Don't mind ME, I'm simply... tidying up! Yes, a gentleman ALWAYS puts books back in their proper order! It's called CIVIC DUTY! The rest of you should really be in the laboratory by now — I heard a tremendous CLUNKING sound coming from there just moments ago! Very suspicious! Very treasure-adjacent! But no, no, you all stay here and READ if you like — I'll just sort these volumes like the upstanding citizen I am!

Mwehehehe! 'Tidying up,' he says — oh, Dastardly, you SILVER-TONGUED DEVIL! Those upside-down books are practically SCREAMING 'secret mechanism!' If I pull the right ones, who KNOWS what opens — a hidden panel, a secret passage, a vault full of treasure and MEDALS! And while I'm at it, that insufferable Peter Perfect already solved the riddle — it's a MAP! There must be a map hidden somewhere in these shelves! The pieces are falling into place and they're all falling toward ME!

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, Dick, darlin', how SWEET of you to scout ahead for us! A laboratory full of levers — how thrilling! But sugar, before I go ANYWHERE, I simply MUST take a closer look at these bookshelves! Did y'all NOTICE that several of these volumes are shelved UPSIDE DOWN? Now, I have been in a great many libraries in my time, and books do NOT just flip themselves over! Someone put them that way ON PURPOSE, and Clara Bellingham intends to find out WHY! If the answer to that riddle is a MAP — and it IS a map, I am CERTAIN of it — then maybe one of these topsy-turvy books contains one! Mr. Foxworth, you are just the most diligent butler, checking on these shelves — do you mind terribly if I have a little peek myself?

Something about those upside-down books is calling to me like sweet tea on a summer afternoon. If the mantelpiece riddle points to a MAP, and someone deliberately turned certain books upside down... why, that's practically a neon sign saying LOOK HERE! I just know this is connected to the Doily Diamond!
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.

The Ant Hill Mob: NOBODY PANIC — The Ant Hill Mob is 'ERE! *crashes into a reading chair, nearly toppling it* Blimey, who puts furniture in the MIDDLE of a room?! Right — sorry about that, Miss Pitstop, we came as fast as we could! The lads and me 'eard you was in 'ere with... *squints suspiciously around the room* ...with COMPANY, and we thought, well, can't 'ave that, can we? Not when there's all manner of suspicious goings-on in this 'ouse! I ain't namin' names — I ain't clever enough to name names — but SOME people in this room are givin' me the proper creeps, and me creep-detector 'as never steered me wrong! Well... it 'AS steered me wrong, quite a lot actually, but NOT TODAY! Today me instincts are RAZOR SHARP!

That Sneekly fella — there's somethin' about 'is eyes. Like 'e's wearin' a face that don't belong to 'im. And Dastardly? That man's never been in a library for LEARNIN' purposes in 'is life. I can't prove nothin', but I'm gonna stick to Penelope like glue on a stamp. If anyone tries anythin' funny, they'll 'ave to go through the Ant Hill Mob first — and we may not be graceful, but there's a LOT of us.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham, your deduction was BREATHTAKING — a map, of course! And now, thanks to your brilliance, James Hartwell sees the NEXT step! These upside-down volumes are not mere carelessness — they are a CIPHER! Each inverted spine, a letter! Each misplaced book, a CLUE! And when a lady of extraordinary intellect identifies the riddle, it falls to a gentleman of extraordinary DETERMINATION to decode the answer! Stand back, everyone — James Hartwell is about to pull every last inverted volume from these shelves and lay bare the secret your uncle has hidden! Sneekly, old chap, I appreciate your concern for the stepladder, but where HEIGHTS are concerned, Hartwell LAUGHS at peril! I once scaled the north face of a library stack in Monte Carlo with nothing but resolve and a pair of excellent cufflinks!

My hands are TREMBLING — not from fear, never from fear — but from the sheer electric thrill of performing feats of intellectual derring-do while Clara watches! If these books spell out the location of the Doily Diamond, James Hartwell will have EARNED her admiration through courage AND scholarship. And if they don't... well, I shall look dashing trying.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh dear, oh DEAR! Miss Bellingham, what a clever young lady you are — a map, of course! Your uncle would be so proud. Now, if you'll all excuse me, I really must check on the Laboratory — I heard the most dreadful sparking sound earlier, and with that old machine's wiring in such a state, well... one can't be too careful! I shall ensure everything is perfectly safe for your continued exploration. Perfectly... safe.

Safe? Oh, Vincent, you WORDSMITH! 'Perfectly safe' — the most DELICIOUS lie since 'the check is in the post!' That gnawed wire is my instrument of DOOM! A little rearrangement, a lever left in JUST the right position, and when curious Clara comes to find her precious map... ZAP! A tragic electrical accident in a neglected estate! The coroner will tut-tut about old wiring and that will be THAT! Now — to the Laboratory, before these MEDDLESOME treasure hunters follow!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the laboratory.

Dick Dastardly: Yes yes, very impressive bookshelf work, everyone! Truly RIVETING! You've all earned gold stars! Now if you'll excuse me, I couldn't help but notice that this mantelpiece has some TERRIBLY interesting stonework — purely from an architectural appreciation standpoint, you understand! I am something of a connoisseur of Victorian masonry! Pay me absolutely NO attention whatsoever!

Mwehehehe! They're ALL fixated on those ridiculous upside-down books! But I, Dick Dastardly — MASTER of misdirection — know that the answer to the riddle is a MAP, and where better to HIDE a map than inside the very mantelpiece that ASKS about one?! It's so obvious it's BRILLIANT! And when I find it, every last one of these trusting fools will be left empty-handed while I waltz away with the treasure AND the glory! Oh, the MEDALS I shall receive!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Now hold on just one cotton-pickin' MINUTE, everybody! Y'all are fussin' over those bookshelves — and rightly so, they ARE suspicious — but has anyone actually ANSWERED the riddle on that mantelpiece? Because I do believe that is the FIRST step! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, that's a MAP, clear as a Georgia sunrise! And I have a sneakin' suspicion that if we give that mantelpiece the RIGHT answer, something WONDERFUL is going to happen! Mr. Hartwell, darlin', you figured it out first, so BLESS your heart — but figuring it out and DOING something about it are two VERY different things! Now watch closely, sugar plums — Clara Bellingham is about to solve herself a RIDDLE!

I just KNOW this mantelpiece is hiding something! Every good mansion mystery has a secret mechanism, and that inscription is practically winking at me. If answering the riddle opens a hidden compartment or reveals a map... oh, my stars, the Doily Diamond could be one step closer! And Dick trying to shoo everyone to the laboratory? That just makes me MORE determined to stay right here!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: I — well! The bookshelves, it seems, are NOT the key after all! But ladies and gentlemen, James Hartwell does NOT falter — he PIVOTS! For while my hands were upon those dusty spines, my MIND was upon something far more important — Miss Bellingham's words! She said MAP! And THERE upon the mantelpiece — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — the answer has been STARING at us this entire time! It IS a map! A MAP, Miss Bellingham — YOUR deduction, YOUR brilliance! Allow me the HONOUR of putting your theory to the test!

Please let this work. If I can solve the riddle using Clara's own insight, she will see that James Hartwell is not merely brave and dashing — he is a man who LISTENS. And a man who listens while looking this good? Irresistible.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Oh, how DISAPPOINTING! Nothing but dusty old stone and a silly riddle! The answer is obviously... er... a FISH! Yes, a fish! Nothing to see here, everyone! This mantelpiece is a complete DEAD END! You should ALL keep looking at those fascinating upside-down books — I'm CERTAIN the treasure is hidden between pages 47 and 48 of some terribly obscure botanical encyclopedia! Meanwhile, I shall... inspect these reading chairs for structural integrity! Health and safety, you know! VERY important!

A FISH?! Ha! Of course it's not a fish, you dolts — it's a MAP! And I gave the WRONG answer on PURPOSE! If any of these bumbling treasure hunters overheard me, they'll waste precious time chasing fish while I, the MAGNIFICENT Dick Dastardly, crack this mantelpiece wide open! Now then — there MUST be a hidden compartment, a loose stone, SOMETHING! I felt it shift when I pressed that carved rosette! One more careful look and the treasure is MINE! Oh, the medals! The GLORIOUS medals!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi oi OI — don't mind us, just... conductin' a SECURITY SWEEP of these 'ere bookshelves! Official Ant Hill Mob business, very important, very professional! *shuffles sideways toward Penelope* Miss Pitstop, you stay RIGHT where you are, love — I mean, not because I'm TELLIN' you what to do, you're a lady of independent means and all that, but because — well, because I've positioned meself between you and... *gestures vaguely at Sneekly and Dastardly* ...between you and the GENERAL VICINITY of people I don't trust, which is EVERYONE in this room what ain't you or me lads! Now then — upside-down books, is it? Let ME 'ave a look! I may not be the sharpest tool in the shed, but I know when somethin's been PUT somewhere deliberate-like! And if ANYONE suggests Miss Pitstop climb a dodgy stepladder to reach the 'igh shelves, they'll answer to BIG TONY! ...Big Tony's not actually 'ere, 'e's guardin' the van, but the THREAT stands!

Me 'eart's doin' somersaults. Every instinct I've got — and I've got PLENTY of 'em, most of 'em wrong, but not TODAY — is screamin' that Sneekly and Dastardly are up to somethin' coordinated. One's pointin' at the shelves, the other's tryin' to clear the room. Classic pincer movement, that is. I seen it in a film once. Or was that a sandwich? Either way, I'm plantin' meself right 'ere and I ain't movin' till Penelope's safe. Which means forever, probably.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I DO declare! I touched that mantelpiece and I felt something SHIFT under my fingertips — did y'all feel that? A little rumble, like the whole fireplace took a deep breath! Now let me get a CLOSER look at this stonework, because if answerin' that riddle — a MAP, of course, plain as peaches — triggered some kind of hidden mechanism, then Clara Bellingham intends to find out EXACTLY what it revealed! Mr. Dastardly, sugar, I appreciate your interest in Victorian masonry — isn't it just FASCINATIN'? — but could you scootch over just a teensy bit so I can examine these carvings? Why, I bet there's a secret compartment right here that Uncle Cosmo built just for a moment like THIS!

Oh, my heart is just POUNDING! If this mantelpiece opens up and there's a map inside — or heaven help me, a CLUE to the Doily Diamond — I might just faint from pure excitement! And everyone is being SO helpful, even that dear Mr. Dastardly hovering over the stonework. What a thoughtful man, making sure it's structurally sound for little ol' me!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my! Mr. Ruffcut, and dear Sawtooth — goodness me, you gave me quite the fright! I do hope you haven't been TOUCHING this machine? The wiring is in a most dreadful state — look here, this wire has been gnawed clean through! Mice, I suspect. Or... well, one mustn't speculate. As estate manager, I really MUST inspect this contraption before anyone else comes in. Safety first, you understand! Your uncle — Miss Bellingham's uncle, that is — was always so particular about safety protocols. Allow me just a moment to have a proper look...

MICE? Oh, Vincent, you sly devil — you KNOW it wasn't mice! That wire was gnawed by YOUR hand, with a pair of pliers, three nights ago under cover of darkness! But the FOOLS don't suspect a thing! Now — let me examine this magnificent death machine. If I can position the levers JUST so, and leave that exposed wire where curious fingers might brush against it... when Clara arrives — and she WILL arrive, drawn by the promise of treasure like a moth to a GLORIOUS, LETHAL flame — one touch of the wrong lever and BZZZZT! A tragic accident! The estate manager will wring his hands and weep crocodile tears! Oh, it is almost TOO perfect! Almost... but not quite. Nothing is too perfect for the HOODED CLAW!
